title-group.article-title: Evaluation of an anti-CD3 VHH and construction of an anti-CD3/anti-EGFR bispecific tandem VHH as a cancer cell targeting drug construct

abstract.p: Recently, the development of T-cell engager cancer therapeutics, consisting of anticancer and anti-T-cell antibody parts to engage the T-cell to the cancer site, has gained interest. Anti-CD3 antibodies are predominantly used to achieve specific binding to T-cells for the T-cell engager construction. Various kinds of anti-CD3 IgG clones have been developed and engineered, but the available anti-CD3 VHH, a single variable domain of a dromedary heavy-chain antibody, clones are limited in number. Thus, the assessment of the available anti-CD3 VHHs is important for therapeutic applications. Here, we demonstrated the expression and characterization of an anti-CD3 VHH clone, 117G03, and evaluated this T-cell engager with an anti-EFGR VHH in a bispecific format to assess the developability of this anti-CD3 VHH clone. 117G03 was expressed as a monomer in the soluble fraction and demonstrated decent thermal stability with binding activity against a CD3-positive cell line. The T-cell engager construct was prepared using the refolding method and exhibited enhanced cytotoxic activity against the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-positive cell line mediated by activated T-cells. These results indicate that 117G03 can be utilized for T-cell engager applications.

list-item.p: An anti-CD3 VHH clone, 117G03, has been evaluated.
117G03 showed stable nature determined by thermal denaturation.
Anti-CD3/anti-EGFR bispecific tandem VHH showed cytotoxic activity with activated T-cells.

sec.title: Introduction
sec.p: A bispecific antibody is an engineered antibody that simultaneously binds to two different antigens. Such ability makes the bispecific antibodies an attractive modality for cancer therapeutics [1]. Creating a link between a cancer cell antigen and an immune cell antigen efficaciously recruits immune cells to the target cancer cells. A T-cell engager is a bispecific antibody that consists of a T-cell binding antibody portion and a cancer-specific antibody portion, which has been investigated for therapeutic development. The anti-CD3 antibody, as a T-cell-specific antibody, is widely utilized for the T-cell engager [[2], [3], [4]]. For example, blinatumomab, an FDA-approved drug for acute lymphoid leukemia, consists of anti-CD3 scFv and anti-CD19 scFv [5]. Various studies have used anti-CD3 antibody-based T-cell engagers. On the contrary, CD3-binding VHH, a variable domain of the heavy chain of dromedary heavy-chain antibodies, has not been broadly investigated because of the limited availability of anti-CD3 clones, and a few studies using anti-CD3 VHHs have been reported [6,7]. The T-cell engager created with VHH demonstrates a high potential for use in cancer drugs because the VHH T-cell engager is the smallest bispecific construct and can be expressed by bacterial expression systems, which is also advantageous in reducing production costs. The tandem VHH bispecific constructs are designed by connecting two VHH domains via a linker, and thus, the resulting primary structure is a single chain, which is advantageous for gene construction and expression control compared with IgG-type bispecific antibodies, which typically consist of four different chains [8]. The small size of the VHH bispecific construct may also be beneficial for the diagnostic applications because of its short plasma half-life.

In this study, we assessed the properties of an anti-CD3 clone, 117G03, whose sequence was obtained from patent information. Recently, the utilization of the 117G03 VHH for the bispecific construct was reported elsewhere [7]. Furthermore, we constructed a bispecific tandem VHH construct for the T-cell engager applications. Accumulation of knowledge on the anti-CD3 VHH clones will expand the design of the T-cell engager to create effective cancer therapeutics.

sec.title: Sample preparation
sec.p: Synthetic Genes for 117G03 and 117G03-Ia1 tandem VHH were obtained from Genscript Japan as cloned vectors into pET28 with codon optimization for E. coli expression. The vectors were transformed into the E. Coli strain, BL21(DE3) and the cells were cultured using the 500 mL LB medium with isopropyl β-d-thiogalactopyranoside (IPTG) induction of 1 mM at 28 °C for 16 h. Then, the cells were collected by centrifugation (6800×g, 20 min, 4 °C) and suspended with a 50 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.0, 200 mM NaCl buffer (30 mL). The cell suspension was disrupted by sonication and the pellet was removed by centrifugation (14,200×g, 30 min, 4 °C). The supernatant was applied onto a Ni-NTA column and eluted with 500 mM imidazole, 50 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.0, and 200 mM NaCl buffer. The 15 mL of the eluted fraction was dialyzed against thrombin cleavage buffer (500 mL, 10 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.0, 150 mM NaCl, 2.5 mM CaCl2). Thrombin cleavage was conducted by adding the thrombin (0.2 U/1 mg protein) and incubated at room temperature for 16 h. After thrombin cleavage, the sample was loaded onto the Ni-NTA column, and a flowthrough fraction was collected. The sample was dialyzed twice to 500 mL of phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) buffer after thrombin cleavage. The tandem VHH samples were prepared using the refolding method. The cell pellet after sonication was solubilized by 8 M urea and 50 mM Tris-HCl pH of 8.0 buffer at room temperature overnight. The solubilized sample solution was dialyzed against 500 mL of 50 mM phosphate pH 7.0 and 150 mM NaCl buffer three times at 4 °C for 12 h. The aggregates were then removed by centrifugation, and the refolded sample solution was applied to the Ni-NTA column for purification similar to the soluble expression described above. FITC labeling of 117G03: 1.5 mg/mL (94 μM) protein sample in 10 mM Tris-HCl pH8.0, 150 mM NaCl buffer, and 1.0 mg/mL (2.6 mM) FITC-I (TCI CHEMICAL TRADING CO., LTD.) in DMSO were mixed in a 10:1 vol ratio (1:2.8 M ratio), and kept 8 h at 4 °C, then dialyzed against PBS buffer. Structure prediction was conducted with the Alphafold server running Alphafold3 (https://alphafoldserver.com/).

sec.title: Analytical size-exclusion chromatography measurements
sec.p: A superdex75 10/300 GL column was utilized in PBS at room temperature. Flowrate was set to 0.5 mL/min. Samples of 100 μL with a concentration of 100 μM were loaded onto the column and detected at 280 nm absorption with a Bio-rad NGC chromatography system (Bio-rad Inc.).

sec.title: Differential scanning fluorometry (DSF)
sec.p: Protein thermal stability measurements by DSF were conducted with a StepOne real-time PCR system (Applied Biosystems). The protein concentration was set to 0.1 mg/mL in PBS buffer. The samples were mixed with SYPRO Orange dye (Sigma Aldrich; 250 times dilution). Each sample of 25 μL was loaded onto a 48-well sample plate. Samples were heated from 25 °C to 99 °C.

sec.title: Circular dichroism measurements (CD)
sec.p: Far-UV CD spectra were measured with a CD spectrometer J-820 (JASCO, Japan) at 25 °C. The protein concentrations were set to 10 μM in a phosphate buffer of 50 mM with NaCl of 150 mM at a pH of 7.0. Measurements were performed with a 1-mm quartz cell, and the bandwidth was set to 5 nm.

sec.title: Flow cytometry
sec.p: HPB-ALL (CD3+) of 106 cells (obtained from Cell Resource Center for Biomedical Research, Tohoku University; ID: TKG 0199) were incubated for 10 min with FITC-labeled 117G03 of 30 nM in 100 μL PBS on ice for flow cytometry analyses. The PBS-suspended cells were utilized for the analysis with an RF-500 flow cytometry machine (Sysmex, Kobe, Japan) after washing the cells with PBS twice. The analyses used cell suspensions of 100 μL for each measurement. FCSalyzer software (Souceforge; https://sourceforge.net/projects/fcsalyzer/) was utilized to analyze the collected data. Anti-CD3 IgG FITC (Proteintech Group, Inc., IL, USA) was used as a positive control. All centrifugation steps for mammalian cells were performed at 160×g for 5 min at room temperature.

sec.title: Cytotoxicity assay
sec.p: T-LAK cells, activated T-cells, were induced as previously described [13,14]. Briefly, peripheral blood mononuclear cells (CTL-UP1 uncharacterized PBMC) were cultured for 48 h at a density of 1 × 106 cells/mL in a medium supplemented with recombinant human interleukin 2 (Shionogi Pharmaceutical Co.) of 100 IU/mL in a culture flask (A/S Nunc) pre-coated with anti-CD3 monoclonal antibody (10 μg/mL). The in vitro growth inhibition of cancer cells using EGFR-positive TFK-1 cells (obtained from Cells Resource Center Biomedical Research, Tohoku University; ID: TKG 0367) [15] was assayed with an MTS assay kit (CellTiter 96® AQueous Non-Radioactive Cell Proliferation Assay; Promega) with the E/T ratio set to 2 (TFK-1 cells: 5 × 103/well, T-LAK cells: 1 × 104 cells/well) and a co-incubation time of 24 h. PBS-incubated wells were used for a 100 %-cytotoxicity reference because this treatment kills all the cancer cells during the incubation time and medium-incubated wells were used for a 0 %-cytotoxicity reference. The cytotoxicity values at each protein concentration were calculated as the average of four replicates, and the error bars represent the standard deviation.

sec.title: Construction of the anti-CD3 VHH
sec.p:
We obtained the sequence of the anti-CD3 117G03 VHH from a patent, WO2016/180982. Fig. 1A illustrates the amino acid sequence of the anti-CD3 VHH, 117G03. The structure prediction of 117G03 was performed with Alphafold3. Fig. 1B shows the resulting structure. The predicted structure demonstrates each CDR loop packed side-by-side to form the antigen recognition surface. The CDR3 loop consists of 15 amino acids, according to Chothia numbering, and forms a relatively large surface area for CD3 binding. We could not obtain well-converged complex structures with CD3 using Alphafold3 thus far, parameter fine-tuning may enable the prediction of complex structures in the future.Fig. 1
(A) Amino acid sequence of 117G03 VHH. Three CDR residues are presented in blue (CDR1), orange (CDR2), and red (CDR3). CDR positions were identified by Chothia numbering at the AbRSA server (http://aligncdr.labshare.cn/aligncdr/index.html) [9]. (B) Alphafold3-predicted structure of 117G03. The colors of CDR loops are indicated similarly (A). Left: side view with stick-model CDR residues. Right: top view with sphere model CDR residues. (C) SDA-PAGE gel image of the expression and Ni-NTA purification. The black arrow denotes the band position following purification (1: insoluble fraction after sonication, 2: supernatant after sonication, 3: flow-through fraction, 4: wash fraction, and 5: elute fraction).Fig. 1

A plasmid with the synthetic 117G03 gene was transformed and expressed with an Escherichia coli expression system. The hexahistidine tag was utilized for the Ni-NTA purification (Fig. 1C). The expression yield was 2.2 mg for 1-L culture.

sec.title: 117G03 VHH evaluations
sec.p:
The size-exclusion chromatography analysis revealed that the purified 117G03 was predominantly monomeric with a trace amount of dimer (Fig. 2A). A nonspecific interaction through a hydrophobic surface patch could cause the small dimer formation. Thermal stability measurements using differential scanning fluorometry (DSF) revealed that 117G03 unfolded with a single transition at 70.9 °C (±0.13 °C) (Fig. 2B), within the typical melting temperature range for single domain VHHs [10,11]. We also confirmed that the stability of 117G03 is not changed at different concentration range (50 mM–300 mM NaCl) and neutral pHs (pH 6.5, pH 7.0, and pH 7.5) (Table 1). The stable nature of VHH is preferable for several application purposes, such as the T-cell engager construction. The Circular dichroism (CD) demonstrated a typical spectrum of immunoglobulin folds, indicating the successful preparation (Fig. 2C). Flow cytometry analyses were conducted to confirm the binding activity of 117G03. We performed fluorescein isothiocyanate (FITC) labeling against the purified 117G03 sample. Fig. 2D illustrates the SDS-PAGE image of FITC-labeled 117G03 observed under ultraviolet (UV) light. The observed fluorescent band denotes successful labeling. The flow cytometry analysis was conducted using an HPB-ALL CD3-positive cell line, which was developed from human T-cell leukemia (Fig. 2E). Fluorescent enhancement for the cells incubated with FITC-labeled 117G03 was observed in the flow cytometry analyses, indicating the binding of 117G03 to the CD3-positive cell line. Overall, 117G03 VHH exhibited favorable properties for protein engineering applications.Fig. 2

sec.title: Construction of the anti-CD3-anti-EGFR tandem VHH
sec.p:
We then constructed a bispecific construct of the T-cell engager fused with the anti-epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) VHH, Ia1 (Fig. 3A). Ia1is a VHH clone that specifically binds to EGFR, and we previously demonstrated the construction of a bispecific tandem VHH construct using Ia1 [12]. The N-terminus 117G03 VHH was fused with the C-terminus Ia1 VHH via the G1 linker. The tandem VHH, 117G03-Ia1, was expressed mostly in the insoluble fraction in E. coli strain (Fig. 3A, lane 1). Thus, we prepared the sample utilizing the refolding method. Ni-NTA purification was performed after refolding (Fig. 3A). The purified sample was subjected to size-exclusion chromatography analysis (Fig. 3B). The 117G03-Ia1 sample was eluted at a lower elution volume position with a monodisperse profile compared with 117G03, indicating a tandem VHH structure formation. Thermal stability analysis with DSF revealed a Tm temperature of 63.6 °C (±0.32 °C), which is 10.8 °C lower than that of 117G03. The thermal transition is mostly a single peak, indicating a cooperative unfolding transition. We initially expected to observe two transition peaks that correspond to two independent VHHs in the tandem construct, but 117G03-Ia1 unfolds as if it consists of a single domain. The tandem VHH includes the 117G03 portion on its N-terminal side; thus, the Ia1 portion may be denatured first and induce the unfolding of the 117G03 portion cooperatively.Fig. 3
(A) Expression and purification of the 117G03-Ia1 tandem VHH. A schematic illustration of 117G03-Ia1 is shown on the left. Green: 117G03 part, light blue: Ia1 part. Right: SDS-PAGE results. M: molecular weight marker, 1: cell pellet fraction after sonication, 2: supernatant fraction after sonication, 3: refolded sample, 4: flowthrough, 5: wash, 6: elution fractions of the Ni-NTA purification of the refolded sample. (B) Elution profiles of the size-exclusion chromatography. Red line: An elution profile of 117G03-Ia1, blue line: 117G03 (control). (C) DSF results for 117G03-Ia1. (D) Cytotoxicity assay using activated T-cell (T-LAK) against the EGFR-positive cancer cell line. 117G03-Ia1 data are indicated with green circles. The result for only T-LAK is presented with a red circle. Standard deviations are indicated with error bars.Fig. 3

sec.title: Cytotoxicity assay
sec.p: We then assessed the cytotoxic activity of 117G03-Ia1 via the engagement of activated T-cells with cancer cells (Fig. 3D). EGFR-positive TFK-1 cells were cultured with activated T-cells (T-LAK cells) in the presence of various concentrations of 117G03-Ia1. The cytotoxicity increased over 10 pM, and at the 100 pM condition, the cytotoxicity reached over 90 %. This result demonstrates that 117G03-Ia1 can engage activated T-cells near the cancer cells to enhance effective cell killing via bispecific bridging activity. Thus, the anti-CD3 activity of 117G03 is promising for T-cell engager applications. Previously, we reported the intein-mediated construction method for the bispecific tandem VHH [12]. Using such combinatorial methods, 117G03 VHH could potentially be connected to various anticancer VHH clones to find effective combinations for the T-cell engager.
